title: Nano-tiering experiments scratchpad
content:
Goal: quick, intuition-first set of micro-tier experiments for low-touch SMB & hobbyist flows. Keep things cheap/simple for <10k MAU seed projects, but don't incentivize abusive high-throughput workloads. This is a personal scratchpad — lots of heuristics and TODOs.

Assumptions (back-of-envelope):
- GPU cost baseline: use amortized per-token cost from infra team: 1 GPU-hour ~ $3.50 (spot blended) for inference on 8-bit quantized medium model. This maps to ~ 5M tokens/hour in steady streaming workloads (conservative). => infra token-cost = $3.50 / 5e6 = $0.0000007 / token (~0.70 $/M tokens).
- Add infra overhead (orchestration, storage, network, support) x1.6 => unit cost ~ $1.12 /M tokens.
- Payment processor + margins + churn buffer => target gross margin target 65% => suggested price per M tokens = cost / (1 - margin) = 1.12 / 0.35 = ~$3.20 /M tokens. Round to simple numbers.

User behavior estimates (for small tiers):
- Typical hobbyist: 20 API calls/day, avg request 300 tokens in + 200 tokens out = 500 tokens/call => 10k tokens/day ~ 300k tokens/month.
- Small startup dev: 200 calls/day -> 100k tokens/day -> 3M tokens/month.
- Sandbox heavy: spike bursts are important; need burst cap for < 1 hour windows.

Tier sketches (for experiment matrix):
1) Nano (free-ish): 500k tokens/month included, 30 req/min burst to throttle, email-only support. Add-on packs available.
2) Sprout (entry): $5 / month => 1.5M included tokens, soft rate-limit 60 req/min, no SLA, basic analytics. Overage: $5 /M tokens.
3) Builder (most likely convert): $25 / month => 10M included tokens, 250 req/min, basic SLA, webhook retries, monthly usage analytics. Overage: $3 /M tokens.
4) Scale (paid, committed): $250 /mo => 200M included tokens, dedicated burst pool 1k req/min, 99.9% availability target (hosted). Overage: $1.8 /M tokens or discounted add-on reserved capacity.

Rationale behind numbers:
- Nano free cap chosen to cover typical hobbyist exploratory usage (~300k/mo). 500k avoids early-day blocking and increases virality potential.
- Sprout price anchored to $5 because perceived low friction; included tokens priced at ~ $3.33 /M (5$/1.5M) which is slightly above suggested retail $3.2/M but cheap enough. Overage high to nudge to upgrade.
- Builder is the 'trials convert' tier: effective price = $2.5 /M across included 10M at $25 => attractive cost, gets dev teams comfortable.
- Scale is for small teams who want predictable spend and capacity; economically justified vs payg if sustained.

Burst mechanics & abuse control (sketch):
- Each account gets a token refill bucket per minute computed from included tokens * burst factor. For nano/sprout, burst factor lower (x3 of steady qps), for builder x8, for scale negotiable.
- Rate-limit circuit-breaker: sustained QPS > allowed for >10s => throttle to baseline. Spikes <10s allowed.
- Protect free tier via fingerprinting and progressive verification: email -> phone -> card for larger bursts.

Alternate anchoring: session-bundles vs tokens
- Session-bundle: useful for voice/chat where tokens correlate poorly per 'interaction'. A session bundle = 1,000 tokens equiv. Offer small pack pricing (e.g., 50 sessions / month) for UX-focused apps.
- Hybrid: include N sessions + M tokens. Sessions consume tokens once threshold crossed. Complexity tradeoff: easier to think about UX vs harder billing engine.

Experiment matrix to run (short-term):
A) A/B pricing test: Sprout $5 with 1.5M vs SproutPro $8 with 4M included. Measure upgrade rates & retention over 30 days.
B) Free cap change: free 500k vs free 750k (narrow experiment to see activation lift). Watch abuse pattern (ratio of accounts with >1M usage).
C) Overage elasticity: set overage at $5 /M vs $3 /M for Builder and observe churn/upgrade.

Quick sensitivity calcs (for ops):
- Break-even tokens per month per paying account (consider blended margin): if price = $25 and unit cost = 1.12/M tokens => at $25 you can support ~22.3M tokens before cost eats revenue (25 / 1.12 * 1M = 22.3M tokens). But we target usage lower, so 10M included is safe.
- If average Builder payload = 10M tokens/mo and 10k accounts => infra spend = 10M * 10k * 1.12/1e6 = $112k/month. Revenue = 25 * 10k = $250k/month => gross margin ~ 55% (below 65 target) — need to tighten or upsell.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Validate infra token cost with infra team: is 5M tokens/hour realistic across models (mix of short/long seq)? get per-model profiles.
- How to implement session bundles in billing platform? estimate engineering effort.
- Decide whether free tier should persist on account-level or per-project-level (billing vs org).
- Edge-case: chat apps that use large context windows (50k) — how to price? Consider 'context surcharge' or per-context-block pricing.

Notes to self: keep the pricing language simple on the landing page — round numbers, emphasize included tokens and burst capacity. For first experimental launch, keep overage intentionally punitive to push upgrades rather than risk large pay-as-you-go churn.

Slack refs: convo in #pricing from 2025-10-29 — Jonah posted activation benchmarks. See JIRA-PRC-548 for rollout infra work.

End of scratchpad. Will iterate after infra cost check and A/B test results.
